purpose: This report summarizes a pharmacogenomic (PGx) panel that cross-references the patient's genotype at 87 pharmacologically relevant loci against published gene-drug outcome studies, PharmGKB/CPIC annotations, and FDA drug labeling. It predicts likely efficacy and toxicity/side-effect risk across 44 medications used in depression, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, epilepsy, ADHD, and anxiety. This is a decision-support tool, not a diagnosis. It does not indicate which condition(s) the patient has — it reports how the patient's genotype is expected to interact with a broad library of medications so a clinician can weigh options for whichever condition is being treated.

metabolizer_profile.impact: Methylphenidate – reduced efficacy signal; gene also governs risperidone, TCAs, many SSRIs
Citalopram – moderate response; caution with standard dosing
Clozapine – moderate response; Perampanel – reduced efficacy
Chlorpromazine – increased toxicity risk; Carbamazepine – favorable efficacy
Lamotrigine, phenytoin, primidone, valproic acid – reduced efficacy signal

antipsychotics.finding: One allele favorable / one reduces response
Weight-gain risk signals in both directions

mood_stabilizers_antiepileptics.finding: Good response predicted by two independent genes

adhd_stimulants.finding: Increased risk of social-withdrawal side effects

priority_safety_flags.risk: Increased suicidal-ideation risk during treatment with clomipramine, lithium, nefazodone, paroxetine, or venlafaxine
Increased suicidal-thought risk specifically on paroxetine
Increased risk of adverse reactions to sertraline
Reduced response to valproic acid, phenytoin, and carbamazepine in epilepsy
Increased risk of social-withdrawal side effects on both first-line ADHD stimulants (dextroamphetamine, methylphenidate)

boxed_warning_note: All standard FDA boxed warnings for antidepressant-associated suicidality in young patients, and for antipsychotic-associated mortality risk in dementia-related psychosis, continue to apply independent of these genetic findings.

clinical_conclusion.impression: Patient01's pharmacogenomic profile is most notable for (1) intermediate-to-poor metabolizer status across five separate CYP enzymes (2D6, 2C19, 2C9, 2B6, 3A5), which broadly predicts atypical drug clearance and a higher likelihood of dose-related side effects or subtherapeutic response across multiple drug classes rather than any single agent; and (2) two independently derived genetic markers (FKBP5, HTR1B) that flag an elevated risk of treatment-emergent suicidal ideation specifically on paroxetine and, more broadly, on clomipramine, lithium, nefazodone, and venlafaxine. On the efficacy side, the profile is more favorable for lithium (concordant signal from two independent genes, GSK3B and ADCY1), for the SCN1A-linked antiepileptics (clobazam, ethosuximide, lamotrigine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine), and for clozapine and quetiapine among the antipsychotics. Taken together, this pattern is consistent with a patient for whom standard first-line SSRI or first-line antiepileptic dosing may underperform or be poorly tolerated, and for whom paroxetine specifically carries an elevated genetically-informed suicidality signal that should prompt either avoidance or enhanced monitoring if prescribed.

recommendations.action: Avoid or use with heightened monitoring
recommendations.detail: Paroxetine (dual suicidality signal); sertraline at standard dose (CYP2B6 intermediate metabolizer)
Lithium (concordant efficacy signal); SCN1A-favorable antiepileptics; clozapine/quetiapine among antipsychotics

recommendations.action: Dose with caution / consider therapeutic drug monitoring
recommendations.detail: Valproic acid, carbamazepine, phenytoin, lamotrigine, primidone (multiple reduced-efficacy / toxicity signals via CYP3A4, CYP1A1, CYP2C9)
Re-confirm the low-depth PLAGL1 (olanzapine) call with repeat sequencing before acting on it clinically
Interpret alongside actual clinical history, current medication list, and labs — this panel alone does not establish a diagnosis
